title: Applied ML eval-harness onboarding and regression triage playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook documents the end-to-end process for onboarding models into the Applied ML eval-harness, establishing prompt sets and benchmarks, validating quantization profiles, and performing regression detection and triage. It codifies responsibilities, SLOs, required artifacts, and step-by-step procedures to ensure model quality and prevent regressions in production inference.

1) Scope and objectives

- Scope: model onboarding (open & internal models), eval-harness integration, prompt set cataloging, benchmark execution, quantization validation, and regression triage.
- Objectives:
  - Ensure every model entering Redwood serving has a reproducible eval suite and pass/fail guardrails.
  - Detect regressions within defined thresholds and provide a clear triage/rollback path.
  - Validate quantized variants for quality and performance tradeoffs.

2) Definitions and key artifacts

- Eval harness: the CI-driven test harness that runs canonical prompt sets, metrics, and tests for a given model commit/packaged artifact.
- Prompt set: curated input-output examples used for benchmarking and regression tests. Prompt sets are categorized by intent (QA, summarization, instruction-following, safety).
- Quantization profile: configuration that lists quantization recipe (e.g., 8-bit GPTQ) and expected metric deltas.
- Regression alert: triggered when a benchmark metric drops below the defined threshold vs baseline.

Required artifacts for onboarding (each model must include):
- model-metadata.yaml (name, architecture, transformer-size, tokenizer, baseline-version)
- baseline-eval-report.json (latest green baseline metrics)
- canonical-prompt-sets (directory with README and labels)
- quantization-profiles.yaml (if quantized variants are provided)
- integration-tests.yaml (smoke tests for inference correctness and tokenization)

3) Ownership and roles

- Model owner: delivers artifacts, answers triage questions, and coordinates fix deployments.
- Applied ML team: reviews prompt sets, runs eval-harness jobs, approves quantization profiles.
- SRE / Serving runtime: validates performance profiles (latency/cost) and approves deployment to canary.
- Reliability On-call: monitors production alerts and participates in regression postmortem.

4) Onboarding procedure (step-by-step)

1. Pre-submission checklist (model owner)
   - Complete model-metadata.yaml and baseline-eval-report.json.
   - Curate prompt sets: minimum 3 prompt sets covering common intents + at least 200 examples for high-risk categories (summaries, instruction-following).
   - Add tokens/safety labels for prompts that exercise content policy.
2. Submit PR to repo: eval-harness/models/<model-name>/ with artifacts. Include a high-level changelog.
3. Automated CI: eval-harness will run:
   - Unit tokenization tests (integration-tests.yaml)
   - Full benchmark run on small sample prompt sets (smoke run)
   - Metric collection: exact-match, rouge, bleu, perplexity, hallucination-rate, toxicity-score (from safety-scoring pipeline)
4. Review (Applied ML): human review of prompt sets & review of smoke metrics. Approve or request changes.
5. Full benchmark run: schedule on dedicated runners (overnight for larger models). Compare to baseline metrics and record results in baseline-eval-report.json.
6. Canary release (Serving): if metrics are green and performance targets met, schedule a canary in staging for 48 hours. Monitor SLOs.

5) Benchmark metrics and thresholds

- Primary metrics (per workload): accuracy/EM for QA, ROUGE-L for summarization, instruction-following score (human or proxy), embedding-similarity (for retrieval use cases).
- Safety & hallucination metrics: toxicity-score (Perspective/TOX), hallucination-rate (semantic drift detected by reference checks).
- Accepted thresholds (example table):

| Metric type | Baseline target | Regression threshold (fail) | Notes |
|-------------|-----------------|----------------------------|-------|
| QA EM | 74.5% | -3.0 pp | absolute decrease vs baseline |
| Summarization ROUGE-L | 42.0 | -2.5 | relative or absolute per model class |
| Hallucination rate | 6.0% | +2.0 pp | increases are harmful |
| Latency p95 (50 tokens) | 180 ms | +50 ms | validated by Serving team |

- Any metric crossing the regression threshold triggers an automated regression alert and opens a triage ticket (see section 7).

6) Quantization validation checklist

- For each quantized profile provide: quantization-profiles.yaml with recipe, target hardware, expected metric deltas and speedups.
- Run the quantized benchmark suite: full prompt sets + stress tests for long context (>1024 tokens) and KV-cache correctness.
- Compare deltas to baseline and ensure deltas fall within the profile's allowed windows. Example acceptance: ROUGE-L delta >= -1.0 and latency p95 improvement >= 1.6x.
- If quantized model fails quality windows, it may still be approved for low-cost tiers with explicit routing policies and customer-visible labels.

7) Regression detection and triage process

- Detection sources: nightly eval-harness runs, scheduled periodic benchmarks (weekly/biweekly), production telemetry (metrics/embedding drift), and customer reports.
- Automation: failing runs create a JIRA ticket with metadata (model, commit, metric deltas, diff outputs, failing prompts).
- Triage steps (incident-lite):
  1. Assign triage owner (Model owner or Applied ML on-call).
  2. Reproduce locally with exact seed and harness config.
  3. Isolate cause: prompt regression, tokenization change, model weight change, quantization delta, or serving change.
  4. If cause is model-quality regression, revert rollout or escalate to emergency rollback.
  5. If cause is infra/serving, open SRE ticket and optionally apply routing fallback to previous model-version.
  6. Postmortem: a short RCA (1-2 pages) with corrective actions and prompt-set updates.

8) Escalation and rollback rules

- Immediate rollback if:
  - Critical customer-impacting metrics drop >5 pp OR
  - Safety metrics worsen beyond allowed safety window OR
  - Latency regression > 2x p95
- For marginal regressions, apply mitigation: narrow rollout percentage, route low-latency traffic to previous variant, or enable cached-prefix mode for affected endpoints.

9) Monitoring and dashboards

- Each onboarded model must have a model-specific dashboard (Grafana) showing: benchmark metrics, production metric deltas, latency p50/p95, error-rate, and quantization toggles.
- Alerting: regression alert (severity P2), safety alert (P1), latency degradation (P2). Alerts link back to the triage JIRA.

10) Example CLI & CI snippets

- Run smoke harness locally:
  - ./scripts/run_eval_harness.sh --model-path=artifacts/model-v1 --prompt-sets=canonical/qa --out=reports/smoke.json
- Trigger full benchmark in CI (example YAML snippet):
  - job: run_full_bench
    image: redwood/eval-runner:latest
    steps:
      - run: ./scripts/run_full_benchmark.sh --model artifacts/model-v1 --out reports/full.json

11) Retro and continuous improvement

- Quarterly review: Applied ML and Serving runtime teams meet to evaluate common failure modes, update threshold windows, and publish new prompt-set categories.
- Keep a living prompt-set catalog: remove brittle prompts, add real-customer edge cases, and label known flaky examples.

12) Appendix: quick checklist for PR reviewers

- Confirm model-metadata.yaml fields present and accurate.
- Validate prompt sets include expected labels and at least the minimum example counts.
- Check baseline-eval-report references the correct baseline-version.
- Confirm quantization-profiles include expected deltas and hardware targets.
- Ensure CI artifacts link to stored reports (S3/GCS).

Contacts and slack channels:
- #applied-ml (general), #eval-harness-oncall (alerts), #serving-runtime (performance).

Related documents:
- eval-harness standards and runner docs (link in related_pages).
- quantization-profiles best practices (link in related_pages).

This playbook will be updated as the eval-harness and serving runtime evolve. For changes to thresholds or core procedures, create a PR and add reviewers from Applied ML, Serving, and SRE.
